passage:
Dear Preeti,

I'm writing because saying it aloud still feels impossible. Last Sunday I found messages on Nisha's phone. She had been seeing someone else for months.

For two days I couldn't eat properly. I was angry, ashamed, and then I started going back over every conversation, asking what I'd missed, what was wrong with me. I typed a message to her friends to tell them everything and deleted it.

Then your call came, and you didn't ask me to explain. Thank you.

I have decided to make no decisions for a while. I'm staying with my cousin. It was her choice, not something I caused. I can say it, though I don't quite feel it yet.

Please don't tell anyone yet. I only need you.

Jagdish

qa.q: Where is Jagdish staying for now?
qa.a: Jagdish is staying with a cousin.

qa.q: What was Jagdish feeling in the two days after finding the messages?
qa.a: Anger and shame, along with self-doubt, as shown by going back over every conversation to ask what was wrong.

qa.q: What did Jagdish do that was wise, and what could come next?
qa.a: Jagdish decided to make no decisions for a while and leaned on Preeti and a cousin; next Jagdish could keep talking to trusted people until feeling steadier.

qa.q: How might Preeti have felt reading Jagdish's letter?
qa.a: Preeti probably felt honoured to be trusted and worried for Jagdish, and would want to respect the request for privacy.

grounding: Shows the shock, shame and self-doubt of discovering a partner's cheating, with time, friends and the reminder that it was their choice.

passage: You asked what the worst week of my life was. Honestly, this one. I'm Ritu, and on Monday I found out Jatin had been seeing someone else for three months. I saw the messages on his laptop when he asked me to print his assignment. First I felt nothing, as if my body had switched off. Then rage, so much that I wanted to post the screenshots everywhere and message the girl. Then, strangely, shame, as if I was the stupid one for not noticing. By Wednesday I was sure it was my fault: not pretty enough, too busy with exams. My roommate Meenal sat with me on the floor and said, 'Ritu, he chose to lie. That was his choice, not your flaw.' I haven't posted anything. I haven't decided anything about us either. I told Jatin I need two weeks of no contact before we even talk. I'm going home to my sister this weekend. I'm leaning on people. That's all I can do right now.

qa.q: How did Ritu find out about Jatin?
qa.a: By seeing the messages on Jatin's laptop while printing his assignment.

qa.q: What feelings did Ritu go through during the week?
qa.a: Ritu felt numb, then furious, then ashamed, and by Wednesday was full of self-doubt and self-blame.

qa.q: What did Ritu choose to do instead of revenge?
qa.a: Asked for two weeks of no contact, didn't post the screenshots, and leaned on Meenal and a sister.

qa.q: How does Meenal see what happened?
qa.a: As Jatin's choice to lie, not a flaw in Ritu.

grounding: A spoken account of discovering a partner's cheating, feeling shock, rage and shame, and taking time and leaning on friends instead of revenge or self-blame.

passage: Saturday. Vasudha found out from a mutual friend's careless story: her boyfriend Aman at a café in Pune with another girl, his hand on hers, on the night he'd said he was studying. She rang him. He admitted it. She hung up and sat on the hostel stairs, shaking, unable to cry. Jyoti found her there at midnight and didn't leave. Tuesday. Rage had arrived. Vasudha drafted a long post naming him, then a message to the other girl. Jyoti read both and said, 'Write them. Don't send them.' Vasudha deleted them. She also caught herself asking, 'What's wrong with me that he did this?' 'Nothing,' Jyoti said. 'He made a choice.' Two weeks later. Vasudha still hadn't decided whether she would ever talk to Aman again, and she was letting that be okay. She'd been to the counselling centre once. She was eating properly again. Some mornings she still woke up heavy. But she had stopped blaming herself.

qa.q: How did Vasudha find out about Aman?
qa.a: From a mutual friend's careless story showing him at a café in Pune with another girl.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling on the hostel stairs that Saturday?
qa.a: She was in shock, shaking and unable to cry.

qa.q: How did Vasudha handle the urge for revenge?
qa.a: With Jyoti's help she wrote the post and message but deleted them instead of sending.

qa.q: How does Jyoti see Aman's cheating?
qa.a: As his choice, not a sign that something is wrong with Vasudha.

grounding: Shows a young woman who discovers her partner's cheating, moving through shock and rage with a friend's support, avoiding revenge and self-blame, and taking time.
